text:
Production lifecycle support

Scope: Because the platform is unidentified, this describes a typical enterprise-platform approach rather than confirmed product capabilities.

Monitor

- Collect logs, metrics, traces, audit events, user-experience signals, and dependency health data.
- Track availability, latency, errors, throughput, capacity, security events, and business outcomes against service objectives.
- Use dashboards, anomaly detection, and actionable alerts to identify problems and initiate incident workflows.

Maintain

- Manage incidents through triage, diagnosis, remediation, communication, and post-incident review.
- Apply patches, dependency upgrades, certificate rotation, database maintenance, backups, recovery tests, and capacity adjustments.
- Detect configuration drift, vulnerabilities, policy violations, expiring integrations, and unsupported components.

Enhance

- Convert feature requests and operational findings into a prioritized backlog with traceability to affected services and requirements.
- Deliver changes through automated build, security, test, approval, deployment, and rollback controls.
- Use feature flags, canary releases, or phased rollouts to reduce risk and verify behavior before broad release.

Continuously improve

- Analyze incidents, performance trends, support tickets, user feedback, and business metrics to identify improvement opportunities.
- Tune performance, reliability, cost, usability, security, and operational automation based on measured results.
- Feed lessons into architecture decisions, tests, runbooks, standards, service objectives, and future roadmap priorities.

This creates a closed loop: production telemetry and feedback reveal needs, prioritized changes pass through controlled delivery, and post-release measurements confirm whether each change improved the application.
limitations: The platform’s actual monitoring, automation, deployment, governance, and security capabilities cannot be confirmed without its identity.
